gap7_completion.rationale: The calm-gap gate reads the 07:00 ET price from RH bars, and RH only emits a bar for a minute in which the name actually traded. A name that is merely QUIET at 07:00 therefore has no bar, and the ranker -- which fails conservative by design -- reports CALM-GAP FAIL. That is the right default for a missing input but it is not a statement about the gap: it disqualifies a name for being illiquid at 07:00 rather than for gapping too hard. Day 19 lost MOVE exactly this way.
gap7_completion.feed_discipline: Parity fix #8 forbids carrying a threshold across feeds because premarket VOLUME differs ~4x between RH and Polygon. That argument is about volume. The calm gap is a PRICE RATIO against the prior close and the feeds agree to the cent -- confirmed here: Polygon's last AMCI print at/before 07:00 is 06:45 at 4.4083, byte-identical to RH's 06:45 bar. Nothing was written into the RH bar CSVs; the completion is a ledger fact, not a merged bar.

vetoes._accounting_note: Counted as THREE SEPARATE RULES per the 2026-08-14 finding. A blended rate hides which rule is binding, and the modelled 50-65% optimum from the V-series speaks to the SPREAD veto only -- the depth and chase vetoes have never been modelled. The denominator is ENTRY DECISIONS REACHED, i.e. names that cleared halal, calm-gap, coil and rank and were actually taken to the book. Names refused earlier (halal, calm-gap, fake gap) are NOT veto decisions and must not inflate the denominator.

depth.note: Inside ask was ONE share, next level TWO. The whole displayed ask side up to 42.19 held 3 shares against 357 needed. Sweeping 357 would have to reach 42.62 (1+2+100+500=603 cumulative), a modelled VWAP near 42.54, i.e. ~1.33% worse than the inside ask. A genuine save against the naive fill-at-the-ask assumption.

chase_fill_arming.note: coil 1.000 means last EQUALS the session high, so a stop-buy at the session high has its trigger already met and would convert to a market order into the 1-share book above. This is the Day-5 LFST failure exactly. Per the fill-arming rule the alternative is a marketable limit capped at trigger+0.5% = 42.19, which the book cannot fill (3 shares) -- so the fallback is also a veto, not an entry.

trigger_c.why_not_a_miss: The tag refused it, which is correct, but the deeper reason it was never takeable is that at 11:11 TBN was 41.4779 = +9.5% against a +10% threshold of 41.668. Its +10% cross did not print until the 11:16 bar at 41.83. A Trigger C signal on a name that has not yet crossed is not a legal entry under C37 at all -- eligibility requires the cross to have ALREADY printed. So this is not a polling failure and not a missed trade; it is a signal that fired while the name was still ineligible.

Cadence actually run while flat today was ~15-20 min for the full scan, not the protocol's 5, which is a real deviation and is logged as such.

errors.severity: HIGH -- silent data corruption, caught in-session
errors.title: Cross-day scan_dump filename collision injected FOUR of yesterday's symbols into today's crossed set
errors.what_happened: Dumps were named scan_dump_{HHMM}.json with no date. Day 19 left scan_dump_0724.json (and 0631/0650/0751/0829/0911/1117) in the same directory. At 07:24 the delta-build correctly REFUSED (INBS had fallen off the 07:03 base and no name was supplied) and therefore wrote nothing -- but the sweep that followed read the pre-existing scan_dump_0724.json, which was 2026-08-31's tape, and reported YDDL +49.09%, NEOV +15.87%, ANPA +10.80% and DCOY +10.69% as NEW crossers while marking all twelve of today's real candidates GONE.
errors.why_it_matters: The crossed set is a LATCH -- once a name is in it, it stays eligible until 14:30 -- so this is not self-correcting. Four names whose +10% cross never printed today would have sat in the pool as tradeable candidates for the rest of the session. NEOV in particular was yesterday's actual traded name, so it would have looked entirely plausible on a re-rank.
errors.how_it_was_caught: The sweep printed 'rows=18/18' when the live scan had just returned 73, and the dropped-fund count fell to 0. A scan that is 95 percent ETFs cannot suddenly have no funds in it.
errors.fix_applied: 1) plan/purge_candidates.py written and run -- the four phantoms removed, candidates back to the correct 12, with the reason recorded inside scan_state itself. 2) All of today's dumps renamed to scan_dump_{DATE}_{HHMM}.json, so the namespace can no longer collide across sessions. Day 19's files were left untouched.
errors.residual_risk: Two failure modes combined here and only the first is now fixed: the filename collision, and the fact that a FAILED delta-build leaves a stale file in place that the NEXT command happily consumes. scan_sweep.py should refuse a dump whose mtime is not from the date it is being swept for -- that is a one-line guard and it would have caught this independently of naming.

findings.title: Every halal-clean name's premarket gain evaporated at the opening bell -- the marks were thin-tape artefacts
findings.detail: The four names that survived the halal gate all collapsed below +10% within three minutes of the open. AMCI opened 4.04 against a 4.00 prior close (+1.0%) after showing +10.21% premarket; CLRO opened exactly at its 5.21 prior close after +7.10%; EXOZ printed +7.3% on 105 shares; ILAG did not trade at all.
findings.why: AMCI's entire premarket +10.21% rested on ONE 200-share print at 06:45, and CLRO's +7.10% on 121 shares at 06:51. Those are the same prints this session used to complete their gap7 from Polygon. The completion was methodologically right -- the feeds agreed to the cent -- but a price is only as meaningful as the size behind it, and 200 shares is not a market.
findings.implication: The gap7 completion tool should report the SIZE behind the print it uses, not just the price. A gap7 sourced from a 200-share trade and one sourced from a 200,000-share trade are not the same evidence, and today the distinction was the whole story: both completed names were, in substance, untraded.
findings.second_order: This also explains the halal paradox from the other side. The names that pass the ratio test are small and cash-funded, which is exactly the population whose premarket prints are single-lot noise. So the survivors are not merely wide -- some of them are not really trading at all.

findings.title: The scan can return CRYPTO rows, and every existing filter classifies by NAME only
findings.detail: UNI 'Uniswap' arrived at +11.95% with instrument_type CRYPTO. scan_sweep's three drop patterns (FUND_PAT, NONCOMMON_PAT, SPAC_PAT) all match on the Name string, and no name regex will ever catch a coin -- 'Uniswap' looks exactly like a small-cap operating company. The row would have entered the crossed set as a common-stock candidate.
findings.why_instrument_type_works_here: The tool guide warns that instrument_type is useless for screening because EQUITY covers stocks AND funds alike -- which is true, and is why fund detection has to be name-based. But that argument is one-directional: a value that is NOT EQUITY is decisive. CRYPTO is never common stock.
findings.fix: scan_sweep.py now drops any row whose instrument_type != EQUITY into a new 'nonequity' bucket. dump_from_delta.py was also fixed in the same breath: it hardcoded instrument_type EQUITY on every row it wrote, which would have silently relabelled the coin as an equity and walked it straight past the new guard. It now carries the type from the base dump or takes a !TYPE! prefix.
findings.lineage: Third contamination class found in three sessions: Day 19 found warrants (EOSEW), earlier sessions found leveraged ETFs and SPACs, today crypto. The pattern is that the saved scan filters on price and %change ONLY, so every non-common-stock instrument RH lists is free to appear.

But it is a PROCESS result, not an edge result -- one ticket cannot reach a benchmark that assumes rotation through several.
eod.why_only_one_ticket: Not the one-position rule this time, and not a slow holder -- it is the halal gate. 27 names were screened and 21 refused. Of the six survivors, five were untradeable (SSM calm-gap blocked at +52.6%, EXOZ never traded on either feed, AMCI and CLRO collapsed below +10% at the bell on single-lot premarket marks, TBN triple-vetoed at the book). MMED was the only name all day that was both permissible and liquid.
